label: The advisor's default bars are confidence 0.8 and uncertainty 0.35, set in SKILL_ADVISOR_COMPAT_CONTRACT and overridable through SPECKIT_ADVISOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD and SPECKIT_ADVISOR_UNCERTAINTY_THRESHOLD; a per-model key is missing and would matter only for a shadow model lane.

The Pi hook sets advisorFailed on a thrown advisor error and then delivers no context, so a crash is silent to the model while a timeout gets the fallback directive; the visible-fallback ADAPT applies to both the Claude and Pi hooks (OpenCode plugin unread).

The gate2 golden routing fixture defines only positive expectedSkillAny cases and has no negative-control or abstain rows, so adding the extension's unrelated-control and required/acceptable split is new fixture work.

Consolidated verdicts V1-V20: one ADOPT (recorded-not-inferred history rule), nine ADAPT (shadow tie-break lane, floored-confidence count, negative controls, churn measurement, weak-follow-up guard, visible crash fallback, operator warning, opt-in why fields, static tool floor), ten REJECT (model replacement, global threshold, inventory floor, additive-only, suppression memory, reply text in scorer, fail-closed by name, pins, tool advertisement filter, scored call gate).

Most REJECTs share one root: the extension replaces or withholds an advertisement while the advisor adds a hint on top, so what transfers is measurement, observability and failure visibility, not selection mechanics.

Live probes for the orchestrator: follow-up routing policyReason, Code Mode declared-schema token size, a shadow tie-break log over ambiguous golden rows, a session-keyed flip rate, and the OpenCode plugin's thrown-error path.
